response: Yes, Web-based and clinic samples of gay men living with HIV can differ on self-reported physical and psychological symptoms. Research has shown that these two groups may have distinct demographic characteristics, healthcare utilization patterns, and symptom experiences. For example, Web-based samples may report more psychological symptoms, such as depression and anxiety, while clinic samples may report more physical symptoms, such as pain and fatigue. These differences may be due to various factors, including selection bias, socioeconomic disparities, and varying levels of healthcare access and utilization. Therefore, it is essential to consider these differences when designing studies, interventions, and healthcare services for gay men living with HIV.
